A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, five figures, equations, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching material across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2 experiments on PKU-SafeRLHF in Section 5 and numerical simulations in Appendices B.8–B.9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and simulations in Figures 2–5. Its new Section 5.2 separately discusses results attributed to other studies.

M1.justification: The RLHF, DPO, online-DPO/PILAF procedures and sparsity-regularized reward estimator are retained. Expanded mathematical descriptions and relocated implementation passages do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PKU-SafeRLHF QA, prompt, safer, and better data and the same bandit simulations. Additional datasets named in Section 5.2 belong to cited studies, not new evaluations by this work.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same RLHF versus online-DPO, reward-model versus DPO, and numerical RL/DPO/online-DPO comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Model sizes, data splits, sample-size ranges, freezing conditions, reward scales, and training settings match. The exact versus empirical BT loss, regression surrogate, and online sampling details move to Appendix C without changing.

E4.justification: The reward-scale sweep, model mis-specification conditions, sample-size analysis, and Appendix B.8–B.9 numerical examples are retained. Section 5.2 adds discussion of published studies rather than another original supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds and retain the same plotted uncertainty displays. No repeated-run, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 retain identical plotted results, including their rankings, trends, and uncertainty bands. The numerical examples and original experimental findings also match; no original empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorem 11, formalized as Theorem 15 in Appendix B.11.5, deriving policy sub-optimality bounds beyond v2's reward-estimation separation. It also adds a soft-value decomposition and explicit mis-specification bounds in B.12. A newly displayed surrogate-reward formula in Section 4 omits the reference-policy term retained in Section 2, introducing an inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the case-dependent RLHF/DPO/online-DPO ordering and sparsity-based statistical advantage claims. The new policy sub-optimality theorem supplies additional formal support for a performance consequence already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: v3 expands the mechanism discussion into the 'Curse of value function,' elaborates implications for relative model sizes and sample complexity, and connects specific theoretical cases to existing empirical studies. The stated small-model and alternative-reward-modeling limitations remain.

D1.justification: Code and dataset access information, hyperparameters, hardware, memory requirements, and runtimes are unchanged. Appendix C's additional implementation paragraph reproduces details previously given in Section 5.

R1.justification: v3 adds Li et al. (2025), Razin et al. (2026), and Gopalan et al. (2026), distinguishes the concurrent studies' approaches, and explicitly connects several existing empirical papers to its theory. Its principal positioning relative to Swamy et al. and Nika et al. remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains, with targeted restructuring: Section 3 uses paragraph headings, Section 4 reorganizes the model explanations, Section 5 gains two subsections, and material moves among the main text and appendices. Notation, wording, affiliations, and acknowledgements are also edited.

P2.justification: All five figures are retained. Figure 1 loses its subsection references, the experimental figure block is repositioned, and Figure 4 is enlarged. Equation formatting and surrounding page layout also change.

improvement.justification: Theorem 11 and Appendix B.11.5 better connect the existing reward-estimation analysis to the paper's policy-performance objective, while the expanded mechanism explanation and literature discussion improve interpretability. These gains are tempered by the new Section 4 surrogate-reward formula omitting the reference-policy term, contrary to Section 2. Overall, the revision provides a qualified theoretical and explanatory improvement.
